Headteacher's Welcome
I am delighted to extend a warm welcome to you as the Headteacher of Brymore Academy, a dedicated and inspiring educational setting for your child. If you have not already done so, I would urge you to come and visit us so that you can see what makes Brymore such a special place; the boys themselves!
Academically, we are consistently placed in the top 5% of schools nationally for student progress which is testament to excellent teaching, individualised support and our unique practical curriculum which makes the most of our facilities and emphasis on traditional values.
At Brymore we place huge importance on our 3R’s: Responsibility, Resilience and Resourcefulness.
We develop these by expecting our students to support the running of the school, through early morning and evening farm duties, maintenance of our flower beds, borders and grounds, as well as assisting in key events throughout the academic year. ‘Diligentia et labore’ or labour with diligence sums up the Brymore way.
Manners, respect for each other and hard work embody the traditional values that we look to develop in all our students so that they are well prepared for life beyond Brymore when they leave us. Alongside this, a broad and rich curriculum, as well as an extensive range of extra-curricular activities provide an ‘experience to last a lifetime.’
We are one of only 30 state boarding schools, where boarding fees are relatively modest and education is free. All our boarding accommodation is either recently built or refurbished providing a comfortable home from home, supported by our dedicated boarding team. Students benefit from our 110 acre farm and extensive horticulture facilities including a one acre walled garden where each student can have their own plot, excellent workshop facilities, and outdoor swimming pool, teaching block, gym and a mountain bike track all set in fifteen acres of countryside bordering the Quantock Hills.
We believe in the importance of a partnership between home and school. At Brymore we actively encourage parental involvement in your child's education. Your support in our educational, social and fundraising activities is invaluable and we look forward to embarking on your child’s next stage of education together.
I would encourage you to visit the school and experience our students and staff in action.
Thank you for your interest in our school and I look forward to welcoming you to Brymore.

School Vision & Values
At Brymore, our history and tradition are not just part of the past—they are a vital part of who we are today. We are proud to be custodians of the culture and ethos created by those who came before us. Every student, every staff member, and every member of our wider community plays a role in preserving and upholding the values that have shaped Brymore over generations. Our school motto, "Diligentia et Labore" – through diligence and hard work – captures the essence of what it means to be part of this school. It reminds us that success is earned through consistent effort, determination, and integrity. These principles are not simply words on a blazer—they are lived out daily in our classrooms, workshops, fields, and boarding houses. Underpinning our ethos are the three Rs:
Resourcefulness
Responsibility
Resilience
These qualities are fundamental to the development of every Brymore Boy. We teach our students to be resourceful—to think independently, to solve problems creatively, and to make the most of the opportunities around them. We expect them to take responsibility for their actions, their learning, and their role within the school and wider community. We encourage them to build resilience—to face challenges with courage, to persevere when things are difficult, and to learn and grow from setbacks.
Upholding our traditions is not about resisting change; it is about recognising the strength of our foundations and using them to shape the future.
We believe that creating young men who live up to the standards and values of those who came before them is paramount. In doing so, we honour the legacy of our past while preparing our students to become the leaders, workers, and gentlemen of tomorrow—young men who will go on to become proud ambassadors of Brymore, continuing the story with pride, purpose, and principle.
As a school we have been told repeatedly that ‘you can recognise a Brymore Boy.’ But what is a Brymore Boy? As a school and a staff body, what type of young man are we striving to develop? A Brymore Boy is much more than just a student – he is a living embodiment of the school's ethos, traditions, and community spirit. He is bought in to our culture, embracing the values that make Brymore unique and ensuring they are reflected in both his character and conduct. He is first and foremost academic and engaged, approaching learning with curiosity, commitment, and pride. Whether in the classroom, workshop, or on the farm, he is hard working and determined, striving for personal excellence while encouraging the same in others. A Brymore Boy is passionate about his subjects, his hobbies, and his school, and this passion is balanced by a grounded sense of humility and honesty. As an ambassador for the school, a Brymore Boy is always impeccably presented, well-spoken, and polite. He is respectful, well-mannered, and grateful, understanding the value of opportunities he is given and the importance of representing his school with pride.
A Brymore Boy is also a gentleman – someone who is kind, inclusive, and supportive of others.
He shows tolerance and open-mindedness, always willing to listen, learn, and accept different perspectives. He is a moral individual, guided by a strong sense of right and wrong, and uses this as the foundation for his decisions and actions. He is confident but not arrogant, competitive yet fair, and always a reliable team player. He takes responsibility, shows initiative, and is ready to lead by example as a role model to others. Whether lending a hand to a peer, volunteering his time, or cheering on a teammate, a Brymore Boy is helpful, friendly, and above all, proud of his school. Through his behaviour and attitude, he helps to build and sustain the unique spirit of Brymore, ensuring that its legacy continues for generations to come.

Welcome to Boarding
Boarding at Brymore is firmly based on the core principles of family living. We strive for an open, inclusive and purposeful atmosphere in which students are encouraged to fulfill their academic and personal potential; where individual needs are addressed and achievements within all areas of the school are celebrated.
We are fortunate enough to have a broad mixture of backgrounds among the boarding community; we pride ourselves on drawing on the best of this rich variety and creating an environment that values individuals but offers an experience that is all the better for its sense of collaboration.
As a former Brymore student myself, I am able to speak with confidence and certainty of the positive impact it is able to deliver to each and every student. I and hundreds of former students owe a debt of gratitude to Brymore and the dedicated staff that work here, who continuously strive to make each individual’s experience as unique and positive as possible.
I can honestly say that Brymore is unlike any other school that I have attended as a student, or have worked in as a teacher throughout my profession, it is truly one of a kind. Boarding has played an important part in the history of Brymore School. Many of our greatest alumni were indeed boarders themselves.
For those of us who have lived and worked in the boarding environment, whether currently or in the past, boarding at Brymore has a special atmosphere and character that embraces the qualities of the individuals who pass through our houses. I and all the dedicated pastoral team here at Brymore extend a warm welcome to all boarders and their parents and guardians. We look forward to meeting you in due course and welcoming you to the Brymore family.
Mr Robert Watts

Curriculum Overview
At Brymore Academy we aim to offer students a curriculum that equips them with the knowledge and skills to successfully progress onto further education and ultimately into employment of their choice.
We operate a two-week timetable with 30 periods per week distributed across a range of subjects as seen below. Alongside our ‘timetabled curriculum’, we offer a ‘wider curriculum’ that includes our daily tutor time sessions, enrichment activities, Friday afternoon personal development options, sports clubs, STEM and careers programmes alongside much more.
In key stage 3 we offer a broad range of subjects that are carefully balanced to ensure that all students develop knowledge and skills across different subject disciplines. Across Years 7 to 9 students study our bespoke Land Based Studies course that equips them with applied knowledge and skills in both Horticulture and Agriculture.
Year 10 serves as the formal start to GCSE studies and requires students to select their option subjects from a curated list of subjects. In Years 10 and 11 timetables follow the allocations below. We have purposefully ensured that Year 10 and 11 students receive 2 lessons of PE, as well as 2 lessons of games per fortnight for the benefit of their physical and mental wellbeing.

Extra Curricular, Trips & Activities
Brymore has a strong boarding ethos, which means that a full academic, co-curricular and extra-curricular programme is offered daily. From morning to evening there is a huge amount on offer, whether boys are out-boarders or boarders.
Boys have a vast range of extra-curricular activities to choose from including a comprehensive sporting programme operating during curriculum time, after school and at the weekends. The extra-curricular programme has been specifically developed to engage and enthuse boys interests, ranging from sports, recreational pursuits, engineering and personal development to experiencing the great outdoors, arts and enhancing their cultural awareness.
Major sports are on offer to our students including rugby, hockey, cricket, swimming and athletics. Alongside these there are many other sports also available including basketball, badminton, table tennis, triathlon, volleyball, road and mountain biking, fitness training and archery.
The extra-curricular programme provides pupils with many opportunities throughout their time at Brymore to develop lifelong skills such as leadership and teamwork through involvement in team sports, young farmers club, public speaking, farm and garden duties as well as the running of numerous leadership groups throughout the school to mention but a few.
Throughout the year the extra-curricular programme, which takes place during lunch times, after school and weekends, offers over 100 activities, covering a diverse range of opportunities to become involved in Brymore life including, Lego club, 10 pin bowling, Airhop, cinema trips, welding, engineering, RC car club, fitness , circuit training, cookery, boarding house activities / games and many more.
Every year there are new additions to the programme and as a boarding school we endeavour to match the needs of our students. Brymore has excellent facilities including many pitches, Swimming Pool, Fitness Room, Gymnasium, a purpose-built mountain bike track, forge, engineering workshops, tennis and multi use games area and use of a nearby golf course. The school is set in beautiful grounds providing space for students to unwind, socialise or simply to relax.
Should you have any queries please contact Mr Orr on 07471 564155 or email harry.orr@brymoreacademy.co.uk

School Trips
Every year the school offers a range of trips to the students. These offer as many boys as possible a chance to enhance their understand of the world around them by travelling overseas, awaken their curiosity, feed their imagination and provide a lifetime of memories. These may vary from year to year but current planned trips include:
Ski Trip
Each year, Brymore boys ski and snowboard on the snow-sure slopes of Folgarida, surrounded by the breathtaking beauty of Italy’s UNESCO-listed Dolomites. Thanks to Max Ski’s family connection with the four-star Luna Wellness Hotel, our boys enjoy exceptional accommodation that makes this a truly special school trip. Superb skiing, incredible adventures and friendships strengthened - a highlight boys consistently recall as their favourite Brymore memory.
The trip is open to all year groups and launches each January, with initial priority given to Years 8, 9 and 10.
Iceland Experience
This trip, offered to boys in Years 9, 10 and 11, takes the group to the stunning country of Iceland, an actively volcanic island, situated in the middle of the North Atlantic Ocean.
During our five day visit boys will experience a variety of landscapes and activities, including trekking through a crack in the Earth's crust; seeing a geyser erupt; walking behind a waterfall; trekking on a glacier; exploring the rugged landscape in a 4x4 jeep and relaxing in a naturally heated outdoor pool. Other highlights include visiting an ice-cream farm, shopping in Iceland's capital city, Reykjavik, and visiting an all-you-can-eat pizzeria! .
If we are very lucky, we might even get to see The Northern Lights.

SEND
At Brymore, we are proud of the quality of learning support that we offer to ensure that all boys can achieve in all subject areas. Some of our team support boys in their lessons adapting tasks and working alongside our teachers. The SEND department also provides an extensive suite of interventions that boys may access when needed and appropriate. As a result, boys with additional learning needs achieve above expectations at Brymore.
We place a great deal of emphasis on supporting boy’s literacy skills and run a range of successful intervention groups including morning readers and Thinking Reading – all co-ordinated by our literacy specialist. These groups challenge boys to become more confident in their reading, enabling them to access KS4 courses more easily. In addition, Brymore has a range of interventions to support social emotional mental health needs including ELSA and cooking, as well as interventions targeted at developing social communication and interaction needs including Lego Therapy and Talkabout.
For a more detailed overview of our provision and how we allocate this, please read our SEN Information Report.
Our SEND team at Brymore work exceptionally hard to ensure that inclusion is at the forefront of all we do.
To contact the SEND department please email Brymore.SEND@brymoreacademy.co.uk

Admissions and Open Events
Brymore's success over the years has meant that we are often over subscribed for entry into Year 7. We would strongly recommend, for those who are keen to apply, to attend either our Open Day in June or one of our Open Mornings in the Autumn (see below).
If you are looking to change schools mid-year, please contact Admissions admissions@brymoreacademy.co.uk or call 01278 652369 (select option 1) to discuss further, to see if spaces are available and the process involved.
For information on how to apply for a place at Brymore Academy, go to our How to Apply page.
Open Events
We hold Open Mornings for prospective students in the September and October before starting secondary school.
In addition, our Open Day, on the last Saturday in June, is known throughout Somerset as we combine it with a country fair. With around 5,000 visitors, we are proud to show off what Brymore does best, alongside some of our local producers. The date of our Open Day in 2027 is Saturday 26th June.
It is a great way to have a look at what we do, whilst enjoying a fun day out with the family. Why not follow us on Facebook or Instagram?
